note: Adapted from the original description in Haviland (1898) Observations on termites; with descriptions of new species (Journal of the Linnean Society of London, Zoology 26: 358–442), in English; published under the genus Termes (now placed in Bulbitermes), with the alate, soldier and worker all described. The original suggested that this species and the two adjacent ones might be only forms of the same species. The original’s nest, type specimen number, distribution and plate (Pl. 25) were not entered; the original records the head width as “*8 mm” and “*7 mm”, read here from the context as 0.8 mm and 0.7 mm.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Alate body length 7 mm, head chestnut, legs and thorax near Isabella colour, abdomen smoky brown; head oval, eyes and ocelli large and close to each other, fontanelle narrow and long; antennae 15-segmented; anterior margin of pronotum nearly straight, anterolateral angles only slightly deflexed, posterolateral margins nearly straight; posterior margin of mesonotum rather broadly concave, that of metanotum narrower; wings 11 mm long, ochraceous brown, media nearer the submedia than the subcosta, reaching the wing tip, with or without branches, submedia with 8 branches, reaching almost to the wing tip; hind legs extending beyond the end of the abdomen; abdominal papillae absent. The queen’s abdomen may reach 16 mm, with distinct secondary sclerotization, the cuticle with numerous minute pale spots and hairs. Soldier body length 3 mm, head width 0.8 mm, dark chestnut, antennae 13-segmented, segment 3 longer than segments 2 and 4; nasus thick, conical, red at the tip, its anterior surface not coplanar with the front of the head; mandibles reduced; postmentum shorter than wide; pronotum saddle-shaped, anterior lobe short and raised; hind femur ochraceous brown, reaching abdominal segment 7. Worker body length 4 mm, head chestnut, antennae 14-segmented. Very close to T. singaporiensis, nest larger.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Body length 7 mm. Head chestnut; legs and thorax near Isabella colour; abdomen smoky brown. Head oval. Eyes and ocelli large, close to each other. Fontanelle narrow and long. Clypeus slightly convex. Antennae 15-segmented. Anterior margin of pronotum nearly straight; anterolateral angles only slightly deflexed; posterolateral margins nearly straight. Posterior margin of mesonotum rather broadly concave; that of metanotum narrower. Wings 11 mm long, ochraceous brown; media nearer the submedia than the subcosta, reaching the wing tip, with or without branches; submedia with 8 branches, reaching almost to the wing tip. Hind legs extending beyond the end of the abdomen. Abdominal papillae absent. Sternite of abdominal segment 7 of the female less than half as long as wide; the queen’s abdomen may reach 16 mm in length, secondary sclerotization distinct, the cuticle with numerous minute pale spots and hairs.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Body length 3 mm. Head width 0.8 mm, dark chestnut. Antennae 13-segmented, segment 3 longer than segment 2 or segment 4. Nasus thick, conical, red at the tip; its anterior surface not in the same plane as the front of the head. Mandibles reduced. Postmentum shorter than wide. Pronotum saddle-shaped, anterior lobe short and raised. Hind femur ochraceous brown, reaching abdominal segment 7. Abdomen oval, tergites arched, smoky brown. Abdominal papillae absent.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Body length 4 mm. Head chestnut. Antennae 14-segmented. Abdomen oval, arched dorsally. Nest spherical, only one nest collected, 10 feet above the ground, larger than the nest of T. singaporiensis. Type locality: Malay Peninsula (Singapore, Bukit Timah), type specimen number 20.
